rv.q: A clicker in hand, Sharp advises viewers that he has memorized and will be cueing up some 2,000 slides over the next 80 minutes. Such is the dramatic engine that drives his autobiographical event. A gangling, gleeful white boy in a bowl haircut and black, high water pants, Sharp is a Southern transplant pleased to be perceived as a New Yorker.

The latest innovator is Josh Sharp, a comedic writer, actor, and Upright Citizens Brigade alum best known for playing one of the two long-lost “identical” twins in Dicks: The Musical. His inventive new show, Josh Sharp’s ta-da!, reinterprets the stand-up routine for the PowerPoint age.

Sharp knows it, and he acknowledges that it’s a pretty masochistic thing to do for the sake of theatre. There is a reason for the madness, which becomes clear as Sharp rockets through the slides in increasingly more inventive ways for hilarious payoffs.
